name: MITES Summer
application_window: Early winter (applications typically open in the fall)
eligibility_note: Prioritizes students from backgrounds underrepresented in STEM and/or under-resourced schools.
description: Six-week residential STEM program at MIT for rising high school seniors, with rigorous coursework in math, science, and engineering plus exposure to MIT research and mentorship.

name: Research Science Institute (RSI)
host: Center for Excellence in Education, hosted at MIT
eligibility_note: Open to rising high school seniors worldwide with a strong record in STEM research potential.
description: One of the most selective pre-college research programs globally. Students complete an original STEM research project under the mentorship of working scientists and engineers.

name: Summer Science Program (SSP)
eligibility_note: Rising seniors with strong math and science background.
description: Six-week residential program where students complete a team research project in one of three disciplines: asteroid orbit determination, enzyme kinetics, or genomics.

name: PROMYS
eligibility_note: Open to motivated high school students with a deep interest in mathematical thinking; no prior number theory required.
description: Intensive six-week program in mathematical exploration centered on number theory. Emphasizes discovery-based problem solving over lectures.

name: Ross Mathematics Program
eligibility_note: Strong math students, generally ages 15-18.
description: Six-week immersion in number theory built around open-ended problem sets. One of the oldest and most respected pure-math summer programs.

name: Stanford University Mathematics Camp (SUMaC)
eligibility_note: High-achieving students with strong math background.
description: Four-week intensive program in abstract algebra and number theory, or algebraic topology, with daily lectures and problem-solving sessions.

name: Stanford Institutes of Medicine Summer Research Program (SIMR)
eligibility_note: Rising seniors aged 16+ by program start; must be U.S. citizen or permanent resident.
description: Eight-week lab-based biomedical research program where students work alongside Stanford scientists in one of eight institutes.

name: Telluride Association Summer Seminar (TASS)
application_window: Winter (applications typically due in early winter)
eligibility_note: Rising high school juniors with strong interest in humanities and social sciences.
description: Fully-funded six-week humanities program centered on seminar-style discussion, writing, and critical inquiry.

name: Iowa Young Writers' Studio
eligibility_note: Students currently enrolled in grades 10, 11, or 12 at application time.
description: Two-week residential creative writing program from the institution behind the Iowa Writers' Workshop. Tracks in fiction, poetry, and creative writing.

name: Kenyon Review Young Writers Workshop
eligibility_note: Ages 16-18 at program start.
description: Two-week intensive creative writing workshop emphasizing daily generative exercises across genres.

name: Yale Young Global Scholars (YYGS)
eligibility_note: Current sophomores and juniors (or international equivalent).
description: Two-week academic enrichment program with tracks such as Politics/Law/Economics, Innovations in Science & Technology, and Literature/Philosophy/Culture.

name: Notre Dame Leadership Seminars
application_window: Late winter (applications typically due in March)
eligibility_note: Rising seniors with strong academic records and demonstrated intellectual curiosity.
description: Fully-funded ten-day seminar for rising seniors exploring a major humanities or social-science question in depth with Notre Dame faculty.

name: Bank of America Student Leaders
format: hybrid (paid local internship + week in Washington, D.C.)
application_window: Early winter (applications typically due in January)
eligibility_note: Juniors and seniors; must be U.S. citizen or permanent resident and legally able to work in the U.S.
description: Paid eight-week internship with a local nonprofit, plus a week-long Student Leaders Summit in Washington, D.C.

name: Economics for Leaders
eligibility_note: Rising seniors with strong academic performance.
description: One-week program combining introductory economics with leadership training at various host university campuses.

name: Hutton Junior Fisheries Biology Program
eligibility_note: High school sophomores, juniors, and seniors; especially encourages applications from women and minorities underrepresented in the sciences.
description: Paid eight-week mentorship pairing students with a fisheries professional for hands-on field and lab experience.

name: Columbia Summer Immersion
eligibility_note: Ages 14-18; specific age ranges per course.
description: Non-credit pre-college courses on Columbia's NYC campus across a wide range of subjects; students live in residence or commute.

name: Brown Pre-College Programs
cost_model: tuition (need-based aid available for eligible students)
eligibility_note: Ages 15-18 depending on course.
description: Short non-credit courses across dozens of subjects, taught in Brown's open-curriculum style.

name: COSMOS
host: University of California (Davis, Irvine, San Diego, Santa Cruz)
eligibility_note: California residents given priority but open to all; grades 8-12 at application.
description: Four-week residential STEM program on UC campuses. Students join a 'cluster' focused on a specific research area taught by UC faculty.

name: NASA SEES High School Internship
host: UT Austin Center for Space Research / NASA
eligibility_note: U.S. citizens aged 16+ with strong interest in STEM.
description: Selective NASA-affiliated internship that pairs students with NASA scientists on authentic Earth-observation and space-science projects.

name: Girls Who Code Summer Immersion Program
eligibility_note: Open to students who identify as girls or non-binary; current 9th-11th graders.
description: Two-week virtual program covering programming fundamentals plus an industry speaker series and a culminating tech-for-good project.
